exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Length of a Triangle's Side Using the Law of Cosines

question.text: Calculate the length of the side $x$, giving your answer to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
The Law of Cosines states that \[ x^2 = y^2+z^2-2yz\cos{X}. \] Here, we have \[ m \angle{X} = 66^{\circ},\quad y = 16,\quad z=19. \] Substituting the numbers into the formula gives

\begin{align} x^2 &= 16^2+19^2-2(16)(19)\cos{66^\circ}\\[3pt] &= 256+361-608\cos{66^\circ}\\[3pt] &= 617-608(0.406\,73\ldots)\\[3pt] &= 617-247.295\,88\\[3pt] &= 369.704\,12 \end{align} rounded to $5$ decimal places

Taking the square root gives

\[ x = \sqrt{369.708\,16} = 19.23 \] rounded to two decimal places.

example.title: Calculating the Length of a Triangle's Side Using the Law of Cosines

question.text: Calculate the length of the side $c$, giving your answer to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
The Law of Cosines states that \[ c^2 = a^2+b^2-2ab\cos{C}. \] Here, we have \[ m \angle{C} = 43^{\circ},\quad a = 10,\quad b=13. \] Substituting the numbers into the formula gives \[ \begin{align} c^2 &= 10^2+13^2-2(10)(13)\cos{43^\circ}\\[3pt] &= 100+169-260\cos{43^\circ}\\[3pt] &= 269-260(0.731\,35\ldots)\\[3pt] &= 269-190.151\,96\\[3pt] &= 78.848\,04. \end{align} \] rounded to $5$ decimal places

Taking the square root gives \[ c = \sqrt{78.848\,04} = 8.88 \] rounded to two decimal places.

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Measure of an Angle in a Triangle Using the Law of Cosines

question.text: A triangle has sides $a$, $b$, and $c.$ The sides $a$, $b$, and $c$ are of lengths $9$, $12$, and $18$, respectively. What is the measure of the angle between the sides $b$ and $c ?$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $A\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{align} \cos{A} &= \dfrac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}. \end{align} \]

Here, we have \[ a = 9, \quad b = 12, \quad c = 18. \]

This gives \[ \begin{align} \cos{A} &= \dfrac{12^2 + 18^2 - 9^2}{2(12)(18)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{144 + 324 - 81}{432}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{387}{432} \end{align} \] Therefore, \[ \begin{align} m\angle F &= \arccos\left(\frac{387}{432}\right)\\[5pt] &=26.38^\circ \end{align} \] rounded to two decimal places.

example.title: Calculating the Measure of an Angle in a Triangle Using the Law of Cosines

question.text: For the triangle above, find $m \angle A$ in degrees to two decimal places.
question.explanation: We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $A\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{align} \cos{A} = \frac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2bc}. \end{align} \] Here, we have \[ a=5,\quad b=8,\quad c=9. \] This gives \[ \begin{align} \cos{A} &= \dfrac{9^2+8^2-5^2}{2(9)(8)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{81+64-25}{144}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{120}{144}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{6}. \end{align} \] Therefore \[ \begin{align} m\angle A &= \arccos\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)\\[5pt] &= 33.56^\circ \end{align} \] rounded to two decimal places.
